methods.label: Compare the two meeting intervals
methods.explanation:
The useful comparison is the combined distance the girls run during each interval. Let \(L\) be the track's length in meters. They start half a lap apart and run in opposite directions, so their distances up to the first meeting add to \(L/2\). Between that meeting and the next, their distances add to \(L\): together they must cover a full lap before meeting again.

Their combined speed is constant. Covering twice the combined distance therefore takes twice as much time, so the interval between the first two meetings is twice the initial interval. Sally also runs at a constant speed, so she ran
\[150\div2=75\]
meters before the first meeting. Brenda ran \(100\) meters during that same initial interval. Thus half the track is \(100+75=175\) meters, and the full track has length
\[L=2\cdot175=\boxed{350}\text{ meters},\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary meeting-distance relationships and proportional distances at constant speed.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is identifying the half-lap and full-lap relationships for consecutive meetings. Direct proportion connects those distances to the two time intervals and Sally's distances. The distance-speed-time relationship is the method's supporting quantitative knowledge.

review.mathematicalCheck: The combined distances are L/2 before the first meeting and L between consecutive meetings. Constant combined speed makes the second interval twice the first. Sally initially runs 75 meters, so L=2(100+75)=350.
